status: 겨울철새·나그네새, 해마다 수십 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 갈대밭, 풀이 무성한 습지, 호수 등에서 홀로 지내는 겨울철새이다. 주로 밤에 움직이지만 낮에 활동할 때도 있다. 유럽, 시베리아, 중국 북부 등지에서 번식하고 한국, 일본, 중국 남부, 보르네오섬, 말레이시아 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Eurasian Bittern (Botaurus stellaris), adult as seen in Korean reedbeds in winter (plumage the same all year): forehead and crown black; a broad blackish moustachial stripe from the bill base down the side of the throat; cheeks and neck sides golden-buff; throat whitish-buff with a thin dark brown central stripe and further rufous-brown stripes down the foreneck; hindneck buff barred dark; back and scapulars black with jagged buff edges, the rest of the upperparts golden-brown densely mottled and vermiculated black; breast and belly buff boldly streaked blackish-brown. Thick dagger-shaped bill yellow with a darker ridge; yellow iris; legs yellowish-green.
art.pose: standing still among reeds at dusk, side view
art.scene: Korean winter reedbed at the edge of a lake, dry brown reeds standing in shallow water; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing hunched at the reed edge: black crown, golden-buff plumage, bold blackish-brown streaks on the breast, black back with jagged buff edges, thick yellow bill, short stout yellowish-green legs
adult, head and neck detail: black forehead and crown, broad black moustachial stripe, thin dark brown central throat stripe, golden-buff neck sides with blackish-brown streaks, yellow eye
art.build: Large, thickset heron, about 76cm long, smaller than a Grey Heron but much bulkier than Black-crowned Night Heron. Thick neck usually hunched into the shoulders; when alarmed it stands rigidly upright with neck and bill pointed skyward among the reeds. Bill stout, straight, sharply pointed, a little longer than the head. Legs short for a heron, thick and yellowish-green, with large feet that grasp reed stems. Very short tail hidden by the wings. In flight broad, rounded, owl-like wings with dark-barred flight feathers, neck retracted and feet trailing.
avoid: Do not paint a long slender neck and long legs like a Grey Heron; the bittern is thick-necked and short-legged.
Do not paint white spots or a grey back — those are juvenile and adult Black-crowned Night Heron.
Do not paint a crest or long plumes on the head.
Do not paint a plain, uniform body; the plumage is densely streaked and mottled golden-brown and black.
